A minor trade-wind trough within a retreating trade-wind surge is
expected to bring scattered showers to the region tonight. Guam and 
Rota may see showers earlier than Saipan and Tinian, but satellite 
trends suggest this difference to not be significant enough for a 
zone split. Model time heights show dry mid- and upper-level air to 
continue, so thunderstorms are not a concern for tonight. A ridge
will fill in afterwards, so showers decrease to isolated Wednesday 
through Thanksgiving Day. Then, a wetter pattern with thunderstorm
potential is possible Thursday night through the weekend as a
weakening upper-level low and surface troughing interact near the 
region. Gusts may reach up to 30 mph near heavier showers as the 
trade-wind surge re-develops as well. As of now, scattered showers
top out at 40 percent, so this will continue to be monitored over the
next few periods.

Marine...
Moderate to fresh easterly winds and frequent strong gusts will 
continue tonight, maintaining hazardous conditions for small craft,
so the Small Craft Advisory was extended through early Wednesday
morning. Then, the trade-wind surge is expected to weaken slightly 
on Wednesday before re-developing over the region Wednesday night.
Combined seas of 6 to 9 feet may increase up to 10 feet on Thursday 
night. Surf along east-facing reefs will remain elevated through the
week, producing a high risk of rip currents at least through Thursday
afternoon. Another trade-wind surge is possible later this week, 
which may continue the threat of rip currents beyond Thursday. Those
with marine and surf interests should continue monitoring the 
forecast.

Eastern Micronesia...
The main focus was on the seas and surf. Arno, Majuro continues to
show seas in excess of 9 feet on the buoy observations. Additionally,
a large, expansive trade-wind surge stretches from north of the
Philippine, crossing 130E to past the Date Line, with the surge
centered between 8N and 22N. Additionally, a STR (Sub-Tropical Ridge)
stretches west to east across this region, with surface high pressure
near Iwo To forecast to slide east along the STR while strengthening.
Then, "to add insult to injury", King Tides will continue to elevate
seas and surf. 

For now, we extended the High Surf Advisory (HSA) for Kosrae, and 
the Small Craft Advisory (SCA) at Majuro, while also retaining the 
previous headlines at Majuro. These seas and surf may briefly drop a 
foot or two for both locations Thursday, but this remains somewhat in
doubt. Then for Friday into the weekend, the pressure gradient will 
strengthen as the STR and area of high pressure strengthen, with King
Tides continuing. This will allow HSA and SCA concerns to reappear 
at Kosrae and Majuro, eventually spreading west to Pohnpei. It's 
possible (if not probable) that seas could be in the 9 to 12 foot 
range for at least Majuro by Sunday, and 9 to 11 feet possibly at 
Pohnpei sometime between Sunday and Tuesday, if the current forecast 
projections verify.

Also in the "forecast mix", is an elevated area of low pressure that
was heading toward Pohnpei. However, the 6-layer ALP (All 
Precipitable Water) imagery suggests the various vorticity centers
(not vertically aligned) appearing to be stalling and repositioning,
possibly due to a pair of buffer circulations seen on the 925mb
analysis south of Kosrae and near Makin in the RMI. With that said,
both the GFS and ECMWF show the upper portion of the low north of
10N, but they also show this weakening/dissipating in two to three
days, due to the strengthening STR/high pressure to the north. This
casts some doubt on the precipitation forecast for all of Eastern
Micronesia, so we took a "middle ground approach" in the zone
forecast to resolve these concerns, as we await further forecast
updates from the numerical models.

Aside from the seas mentioned above, look for mainly moderate to
fresh winds to continue at Pohnpei and Majuro, and mainly light to 
gentle winds at Kosrae becoming gentle to moderate by the end of the 
weekend.

Western Micronesia...
Not much has changed from the previous forecast. An overall dry
pattern will continue across Palau and Yap through the weekend. It is
highly encouraged to follow any water conservation steps recommended 
by your local emergency managers.

For Chuuk, dry conditions will continue through Wednesday, with a
brief period Wednesday night of increased showers as a weak trade-
wind trough passes through. Rainfall is not expected to be very 
high, so don't expect much of a change from the current dry 
conditions. Over the weekend, the NET looks to become more active 
over Weno, bringing increased showers to the main islands with an 
inch or so of rainfall possible. Not enough to eliminate the
abnormally dry conditions, so water conservation is still highly
encouraged.
